dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good morning. Please take a seat. What brings you in today?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Good morning, Doctor. I've been feeling increasingly weak and light-headed for the past few weeks, and over the last few days I've also been getting short of breath when I walk upstairs.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: I see. When you say you feel light-headed, do you mean the room is spinning, or do you feel as though you might faint?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: It's more like I'm about to faint. It usually happens when I stand up quickly, although yesterday it happened while I was walking.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: How often is this happening, and how long does each episode last?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: It happens several times a day. The worst episodes last for a couple of minutes, although the milder ones pass more quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Has anything changed recently in your diet, sleep, workload, or medication?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I've been working longer hours and sleeping badly. I'm also eating less regularly than I used to. Nurse: Doctor, his blood pressure is 98 over 62, and his pulse is 104. Oxygen saturation is 97% on room air.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Thank you. Have you ever had blood pressure readings that low before?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: No. I usually have normal blood pressure.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Are you experiencing chest pain, palpitations, nausea, or unusual sweating at the moment?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm not having chest pain, but my heart sometimes feels as though it's racing when I climb stairs.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Do you have any diagnosed conditions, and are you taking any regular medication?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I was told I had mild hypertension two years ago. I take an antihypertensive every morning, although I've occasionally forgotten it recently.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Have you noticed any recent weight loss, changes in your appetite, bleeding, or black stools?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I've lost about three kilograms without trying. My appetite is slightly reduced, but I haven't noticed any bleeding or black stools.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: What about your family history? Has anyone had anemia, diabetes, heart disease, or thyroid problems?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: My mother has iron-deficiency anemia, and my father has type 2 diabetes.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: All right. I'm going to examine you now. I'll check your pulse, blood pressure lying and standing, heart and lungs, and I'd also like to look for signs of pallor or dehydration.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Is low blood pressure the main reason I'm feeling this way?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: It may be contributing, but we shouldn't assume that it explains everything. Your fatigue, exertional breathlessness, weight loss, and tachycardia could have several causes. Relative: Doctor, he has been much more tired than usual recently. He sometimes has to stop halfway up the stairs.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: That is useful information. We'll arrange a full blood count, iron studies, glucose, renal and thyroid function, and an ECG. Depending on the results, we may need further investigations.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Does that mean you suspect anemia?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: It is one possibility, but we need to distinguish it from cardiovascular, endocrine, metabolic, and other causes before deciding on treatment. Nurse: I'll take the blood samples now and repeat his blood pressure after he has rested.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. If you develop severe chest pain, fainting, or significant difficulty breathing while you're waiting, tell us immediately.

tests.question: What is the medical meaning of the term 'light-headed' in clinical consultation?
tests.explanation: 'light-headed' atamasining to'g'ri ma'nosi: boshi aylangan, hushidan ketgudek bo'lgan.

tests.question: Which term corresponds to 'tez o'rnidan turmoq'?
tests.option_a: feel as though I might faint
tests.explanation: 'tez o'rnidan turmoq' ma'nosiga mos keluvchi tibbiy termin 'stand up quickly' hisoblanadi.

tests.question: Which of the following is the grammatically and clinically standard question to ask about the duration of symptoms?
tests.option_a: How long do you having this symptom?
tests.option_b: How long has this condition been bothering you?
tests.option_c: Since what time you have this problem?
tests.option_d: How many days you are feeling pain?
tests.explanation: Klinik anamnezda davomiylikni so'rash uchun Present Perfect Continuous ('How long has... been bothering you?') to'g'ri shakl hisoblanadi.

tests.question: When evaluating acute pain, what is the best phrasing to assess pain character?
tests.option_a: Is your pain bad or very bad?
tests.option_b: Can you describe the pain—is it sharp, dull, throbbing, or aching?
tests.option_c: Why do you have sharp pain today?
tests.explanation: Og'riq xarakterini aniqlashda shifokor ochiq va taklif qiluvchi variantlar (sharp, dull, throbbing, aching) beradi.
